children: Australia’s seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose to 4.6% in August 2026, up from 4.5% in July and above market expectations, according to official labor market data.
The reading represents the highest unemployment rate since November 2021.

The number of unemployed individuals expanded by 28,200 to reach a five-year high of 722,900. The increase in jobless jobseekers was split between full-time searchers, which grew by 15,700 to 481,000, and part-time searchers, which rose by 12,500 to 242,000.

Despite the uptick in the jobless rate, total employment increased by 39,500 to reach a record 14.84 million in August, comfortably beating market forecasts for a 20,000 gain and reversing a revised 15,900 decline in July.
On an annual basis, total employment expanded by 238,100 positions, or 1.6%.
Local financial markets reacted negatively to the mixed labor statistics. The
stocks plunged 1.3% to 8,649 in early deals, while the Australian dollar weakened to around $0.70, touching a seven-week low.

title: Australian unemployment rises to 4.6% despite strong job creation
